sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast episode 209 recorded on November 12th, 2024.

sentences.en: And today with my co-host, Ben, we chat about board games.

sentences.en: Paleo Vet was a game I played with some friends lately.

sentences.en: You are a veterinarian and you are taking care of dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 你扮演一名兽医，负责照顾恐龙。

sentences.en: And every turn, there are five dinosaurs in the middle of the table available to tranquilize and bring back to your veterinary practice.
sentences.zh: 每个回合，桌子中央都有五只恐龙，你可以把它们麻醉并带回你的诊所。

sentences.en: And once they're in your practice, you are healing them.
sentences.zh: 一旦它们进了你的诊所，你就要为它们治疗。

sentences.en: Each dinosaur has some icons on its card to say what it requires to be healed.
sentences.zh: 每只恐龙的卡牌上都有一些图标，说明治好它需要什么。

sentences.en: Maybe an antiviral, maybe an antibiotic, maybe surgery, something of that nature, right?
sentences.zh: 也许是抗病毒药物，也许是抗生素，也许是外科手术，诸如此类，对吧？

sentences.en: There are different things you can do.
sentences.zh: 你可以做不同的事情。

sentences.en: And you roll dice and they're not numbered dice, they're dice with icons on them every turn to figure out what you can do that turn.
sentences.zh: 你每回合都要掷骰子，它们不是带数字的骰子，而是带有各种图标的骰子，以此来决定你这回合能做什么。

sentences.en: You know, the dice have icons corresponding to the treatment icons.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，骰子上的图标与治疗图标相对应。

sentences.en: And the goal is, of course, to bring dinosaurs into your practice and heal them and then release them.
sentences.zh: 当然，目标就是把恐龙带进你的诊所、治好它们，然后将它们放归。

sentences.en: The wrinkle is that dinosaurs aren't very friendly.
sentences.zh: 麻烦之处在于，恐龙可不太友好。

sentences.en: And while they're in your practice, basically, they are tranquilized.
sentences.zh: 当它们在你的诊所里时，基本上都是被麻醉的状态。

sentences.en: They're asleep while you're healing them.
sentences.zh: 你在给它们治病时它们在睡觉。

sentences.en: But their sleep counter is ticking down every turn.
sentences.zh: 但它们的睡眠倒计时每回合都在减少。

sentences.en: When they wake up, they break out and run away.
sentences.zh: 当它们醒来时，就会破门而出并逃跑。

sentences.en: If they are carnivores, first of all, they eat another dinosaur and then they run away.
sentences.zh: 如果它们是食肉动物，首先，它们会吃掉另一只恐龙，然后逃跑。

sentences.en: So far, this sounds like all bad, right?

sentences.en: But then you start to layer on the things like extra points for achieving certain sets of dinosaurs.

sentences.en: Like you can specialize in healing carnivores and that gives you extra powers and extra points, perhaps, or things of that nature.

sentences.en: Whereas a game like Scrabble is actually, you know, very fun.
sentences.zh: 而像《拼词游戏》（Scrabble）这样的游戏，其实，你知道的，非常有趣。

sentences.en: Well, Monopoly is a bad game, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，《大富翁》是个烂游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's what I've heard called, among other things, you know, also besides the fact that it glorifies extreme capitalism.
sentences.zh: 因为我听人说过，除此之外，你知道的，除了它美化极端资本主义这一点之外。

sentences.en: Rent-seeking property.
sentences.zh: 寻租地产。

sentences.en: Rent-seeking, yes.
sentences.zh: 寻租，没错。

sentences.en: It's a 51% game, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个51%的游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is how I've heard it called.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么听说的。

sentences.en: It's like, once you get slightly ahead, it is...
sentences.zh: 这就好比，一旦你稍微领先一点，它就……

sentences.en: There's a positive feedback loop, right?
sentences.zh: 这里有一个正反馈循环，对吧？

sentences.en: So, once you get the idea behind a 51% game, of course, if one person's 51%, then they run away with the win.
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦你理解了51%游戏的本质，当然，如果一个人占了51%，那么他们就会一骑绝尘赢得比赛。

sentences.en: Which isn't...
sentences.zh: 这并不是……

sentences.en: You know, Monopoly has random elements.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，《大富翁》有随机元素。

sentences.en: So, it's not totally true of Monopoly, but it's basically true.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对《大富翁》来说不完全正确，但基本如此。

sentences.en: It's kind of fascinating, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这挺迷人的。

sentences.en: I think I saw online.
sentences.zh: 我想我是在网上看到的。

sentences.en: So, obviously, I have a background in video games, as you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，显然，我有电子游戏背景，如你所知。

sentences.en: A lot of video games fight against that kind of 51% game.
sentences.zh: 很多电子游戏都在对抗那种51%的游戏机制。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of game which is exemplified by...
sentences.zh: 有一种游戏是以……为代表的

sentences.en: One of the first games I know is Super Puzzle Fighter 2 Turbo Extreme, was it?
sentences.zh: 我所知道的最早的游戏之一是《超级方块战士2 Turbo Extreme》，是吗？

sentences.en: Anyway, it's one of these games where...
sentences.zh: 总之，它是这类游戏之一……

sentences.en: Imagine competitive Tetris, right?
sentences.zh: 想象一下竞技类《俄罗斯方块》，对吧？

sentences.en: But not Tetris.
sentences.zh: 但不是《俄罗斯方块》。

sentences.en: It's the one where you're not fitting the blocks in.
sentences.zh: 它是那种你不需要把方块拼合进去的游戏。

sentences.en: You're just letting the blocks fall on top of each other in different colors.
sentences.zh: 你只是让不同颜色的方块相互堆叠落下。

sentences.en: And when different color blocks meet, they merge into larger color blocks.
sentences.zh: 当不同颜色的方块相遇时，它们会合并成更大的彩色方块。

sentences.en: And then you can explode those larger color blocks and send things over to your opponent to deal with.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以引爆这些更大的彩色方块，把东西发给你的对手去处理。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, it's like Pio Pio or a game of that nature, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像《Pio Pio》或类似性质的游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: It's one of these games.
sentences.zh: 它是这类游戏中的一种。

sentences.en: And it's head-to-head, two players.
sentences.zh: 而且它是正面交锋的两人游戏。

sentences.en: It has the very interesting property that being about to win looks the same as being about to lose.
sentences.zh: 它有一个非常有趣的特性，那就是即将获胜的感觉看起来和即将失败一模一样。

sentences.en: It's not a 51% game.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个51%的游戏。

sentences.en: It's a sort of continual comeback game.
sentences.zh: 它是一种不断咸鱼翻身的游戏。

sentences.en: Because if I send you a lot of material, yes, it fills up your side of the screen.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我给你发很多东西，没错，它会填满你那一侧的屏幕。

sentences.en: So, it's a problem for you to deal with.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对你来说是个需要处理的麻烦。

sentences.en: But it gives you a huge opportunity to send a bunch of stuff back to me, right?
sentences.zh: 但它给了你一个巨大的机会，可以把一大堆东西回敬给我，对吧？

sentences.en: So, it works both ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是双向的。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So, it's like, is it not a...
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像，它不是一个……

sentences.en: Does that involve, like, bluffing kind of?
sentences.zh: 这其中包含某种虚张声势吗？

sentences.en: Or is it the strategy...
sentences.zh: 还是说策略是……

sentences.en: Well, it's an arcade game, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一款街机游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: So, things are continually dropping.
sentences.zh: 所以，东西在不断落下。

sentences.en: Sometimes you're getting fuses which set off different color blocks, right?
sentences.zh: 有时你会得到引信来引爆不同的彩色方块，对吧？

sentences.en: And the larger...
sentences.zh: 而且更大的……

sentences.en: So, you might...
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能会……

sentences.en: If a two by...
sentences.zh: 如果一个二乘……

sentences.en: Say you get a two by two of reds, they fuse together into a larger gem in this game, right?
sentences.zh: 比方说你得到了一个二乘二的红色方块，在这款游戏中它们会融合成一个更大的宝石，对吧？

sentences.en: And say you get a two by three, it would fuse into an even larger gem.
sentences.zh: 比方说你得到了一个二乘三的方块，它会融合成一个更大的宝石。

sentences.en: Or three by three, even larger, right?
sentences.zh: 或者三乘三的，更大，对吧？

sentences.en: And the larger the gem gets, the sort of geometrically more powerful it gets, right?
sentences.zh: 宝石越大，它的威力按几何级数增长就越大，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you send over more stuff for large gems, comparatively.
sentences.zh: 所以，相对而言，大宝石会让你发送更多东西过去。

sentences.en: But every character...
sentences.zh: 但每个角色……

sentences.en: This game I'm thinking of had a sort of Street Fighter character selection.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中的这款游戏有一种类似《街头霸王》的角色选择机制。

sentences.en: So, every character you can select in Street Fighter to be your combatant had a different pattern of colors they would send over to your opponent
sentences.zh: 所以，你在《街头霸王》中选择作为战斗人员的每个角色，当你触发某种宝石爆炸时，

sentences.en: when you got, you know, a certain explosion of geMs.
sentences.zh: 发送给对手的颜色图案都是不同的，

sentences.en: You would send over a dozen geMs.
sentences.zh: 你会发送一打宝石过去。

sentences.en: The pattern they get sent depends on which character you picked.
sentences.zh: 发送的图案取决于你选择的角色。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So, what's the risk at the end of sending, you know, you're close to sending something over, but the risk is that they'll be able to do something with that?
sentences.zh: 那么，最后发送的风险是什么呢，你知道的，你快要发送东西过去了，但风险是他们能利用这一点做些什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: You've just sent a bunch of geMs.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚发送了一堆宝石过去。

sentences.en: They are going to fall on whatever gems your opponent already has.
sentences.zh: 它们会落在你对手已经拥有的任何宝石上。

sentences.en: They're going to fuse together into larger gems, potentially.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会融合成更大的宝石。

sentences.en: And then your opponent will be able to set those off and send a ton of stuff back to you.
sentences.zh: 然后你的对手就可以引爆这些宝石，并把一大堆东西回敬给你。

sentences.en: So, this is why it's not one of these games where when you get ahead, you stay ahead.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它不是那种你一旦领先就能保持领先的游戏。

sentences.en: It is a very interesting mechanic of perpetual comeback.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的永恒逆转机制。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That is...
sentences.zh: 那是……

sentences.en: I'm trying to think of other...
sentences.zh: 我在想其他的……

sentences.en: I mean, Scrabble is not completely dissimilar to that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，《拼词游戏》与此并非完全不同。

sentences.en: It definitely doesn't have, like, oh, you're about to win.
sentences.zh: 它绝对没有那种“哦，你快要赢了”的感觉。

sentences.en: You could be about to lose.
sentences.zh: 你可能正处于失败的边缘。

sentences.en: But it affects the strategy that you play in high-level Scrabble.
sentences.zh: 但这会影响你在高水平《拼词游戏》中采用的策略。

sentences.en: When you're down by over 100, over, like, a bingo or more, you start to...
sentences.zh: 当你的落后分超过100分，比如一个“连击冰果（bingo）”或更多时，你开始……

sentences.en: You start to play a denial game rather than a scoring game.
sentences.zh: 你开始打防守战而不是进攻得分战。

sentences.en: So, there's defensive versus offensive.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就分为防守与进攻。

sentences.en: And offensive, you open lanes.
sentences.zh: 在进攻时，你会开辟通道。

sentences.en: So, it's...
sentences.zh: 所以，这是……

sentences.en: You'll...
sentences.zh: 你会……

sentences.en: Any high-level Scrabble player is always looking at where are the bingo lanes where I can score.
sentences.zh: 任何高水平的《拼词游戏》玩家都在时刻观察我能在哪里得分的冰果通道。

sentences.en: And if there's only one, and you're trying to play defensively because you're up by 150, you're just always one at a time closing that lane so that there's nowhere to score.
sentences.zh: 如果只有一条，而你因为领先150分而试图进行防守，你就会一次关闭一条通道，使之无处得分。

sentences.en: And then the next turn, the player will try to open another lane that that that person can't close.
sentences.zh: 然后在下一回合，对手会试图开辟另一条那个人无法关闭的通道。

sentences.en: And the best kind of play is where you fork, where you open two lanes at once, which is unblockable.
sentences.zh: 而最好的下棋方式就是分叉，即同时开辟两条无法阻挡的通道。

sentences.en: Because if you don't have high-scoring lanes, there's no way for you to come back.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你没有高分通道，你就没有办法东山再起。

sentences.en: So, there's kind of things like that where...
sentences.zh: 所以会有类似的事情，其中……

sentences.en: And even certain countries are known for the way that they train.
sentences.zh: 甚至有些国家以他们的训练方式闻名。

sentences.en: Like, I just watched a video on how Nigeria has become a Scrabble superpower because they have this one guy that won the world championship in, I think, 2016.
sentences.zh: 比如，我刚看了一个视频，讲尼日利亚是如何成为《拼词游戏》超级大国的，因为他们有这么一个人，我想在2016年赢得了世界冠军。

sentences.en: His name was Wellington.
sentences.zh: 他叫惠灵顿（Wellington）。

sentences.en: And it's designated in Nigeria that Scrabble's a sport the same way chess is.
sentences.zh: 在尼日利亚，《拼词游戏》被指定为一项与国际象棋同等地位的体育运动。

sentences.en: And so, they have funding for training.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们有训练资金支持。

sentences.en: And now, like, it's in the top 100.
sentences.zh: 现在，比如，它进入了前100名。

sentences.en: There's, like, 40 Nigerian, like, globally ranked Scrabble players.
sentences.zh: 大约有40名尼日利亚《拼词游戏》选手拥有全球排名。

sentences.en: And there's, like, two in the top 10.
sentences.zh: 其中有两名进入了前10名。

sentences.en: Anyways, and they are all known for...
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他们都以……闻名

sentences.en: Or actually, I think they said it's a myth.
sentences.zh: 或者其实，我想他们说过这是一个迷思。

sentences.en: But the myth is that they play very defensively.
sentences.zh: 但这个迷思是他们打球非常防守化。

sentences.en: But actually, the top players, they're just as aggressive as some of the other players.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，顶级选手和其他一些选手一样具有攻击性。

sentences.en: This is interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, I know that you've played Scrabble somewhat competitively.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我知道你玩《拼词游戏》带有某种竞技性质。

sentences.en: I've played one tournament.
sentences.zh: 我参加过一场锦标赛。

sentences.en: You have a deeper than average understanding of Scrabble.
sentences.zh: 你对《拼词游戏》的理解比一般人要深。

sentences.en: Like, I haven't played much.
sentences.zh: 比如，我没怎么玩过。

sentences.en: I've played Scrabble.
sentences.zh: 我玩过《拼词游戏》。

sentences.en: I know how Scrabble works.
sentences.zh: 我知道《拼词游戏》是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: Like, but I haven't played it anything beyond, you know, with the family.
sentences.zh: 但是，除了你知道的跟家人一起玩之外，我没怎么玩过别的。

sentences.en: And that not very much.
sentences.zh: 而且也没玩多少。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I think like most people, I'm vaguely aware that in competitive Scrabble, like, you need to know all the two-letter words and probably all the three-letter words.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我想像大多数人一样，我隐约知道在竞技《拼词游戏》中，你需要知道所有的两字母单词，可能还有所有的三字母单词。

sentences.en: And four and five and six and seven.
sentences.zh: 还有四、五、六、七个字母的。

sentences.en: Whether you know the eights and nines is the question.
sentences.zh: 问题在于你是否知道八个和九个字母的。

sentences.en: But then there's this whole other strategy of actually play space, controlling the space of play.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还有另一整套关于实际棋盘空间、控制棋盘空间的策略。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is not something that is obvious.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一件显而易见的事情。

sentences.en: You know, most people, I think, would find it fairly obvious that knowing all the two- and three-letter words would be an advantage at the end of the game in particular.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我想大多数人都会觉得，了解所有两字母和三字母单词在游戏快结束时尤其是一个优势。

sentences.en: But the actual strategy of play of, like you say, closing lanes or opening lanes or various things.
sentences.zh: 但实际的比赛策略，就像你说的，关闭通道或开辟通道，或者各种事情。

sentences.en: And indeed, the strategy over time of managing your letter bank, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，随着时间推移管理你的字母库的策略，对吧？

sentences.en: To mean that you're not looking for, you're always looking for bingos, I assume.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你不是在寻找，我假设你一直在寻找冰果。

sentences.en: But you're not necessarily looking for them on this play.
sentences.zh: 但你不一定非要在这轮寻找它们。

sentences.en: You might be trying to set up, trying to, you know, try to go down the highest probability path to set up a bingo next turn or turn after.
sentences.zh: 你可能在试图布局，试图，你知道的，试图沿着概率最高的路线走，以便在下一轮或之后的轮次中凑成冰果。

sentences.en: Or hopefully, you know, ideally every turn.
sentences.zh: 或者希望，你知道的，理想情况下每一轮都这样。

sentences.en: But the top-level play is thinking about things like that, right?
sentences.zh: 但顶级水平的比赛考虑的就是诸如此类的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's honestly, even as a, I would say, above average, like, serious Scrabble player,
sentences.zh: 老实说，甚至作为一个，我想说，高于平均水平的、认真的《拼词游戏》玩家，

sentences.en: there was a whole other world of strategy that I did not know existed until I started watching these Will Anderson videos and commentators commenting on Scrabble tournaments that are now live-streamed that weren't,
sentences.zh: 还有另一整个策略世界是我在开始观看威尔·安德森（Will Anderson）的视频以及评论员对现在进行直播（以前没有）的《拼词游戏》锦标赛进行评论之前，完全不知道它存在的，

sentences.en: you know, in years paSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在过去的几年里。

sentences.en: And the things that people do are, it's incredible.
sentences.zh: 人们做的事情简直不可思议。

sentences.en: Like, so that one of the big things I didn't know about was endgame.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道的一大重点就是残局。

sentences.en: Every professional or elite Scrabble player tile tracks.
sentences.zh: 每个专业或精英《拼词游戏》选手都会记牌（tile track）。

sentences.en: So, you know exactly at the end of the game when there's no more tiles in the bag.
sentences.zh: 所以，在游戏快结束、袋子里没有牌的时候，你确切地知道。

sentences.en: You know exactly what you have and what they have, yes.
sentences.zh: 你确切地知道你有什么，他们有什么，是的。

sentences.en: And depending on the board.
sentences.zh: 并且取决于棋盘情况。

sentences.en: Is that something that is purely mental?
sentences.zh: 这完全是靠心算吗？

sentences.en: Are there rules?
sentences.zh: 有什么规则吗？

sentences.en: Are they allowed to write down?
sentences.zh: 他们被允许写下来吗？

sentences.en: No, yeah, you can write down whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 不，是的，你可以写下任何你想写的东西。

sentences.en: So, all players have, like, a little thing where they just scratch off the letters one by one.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有玩家都有一个小本本，他们把字母一个接一个划掉。

sentences.en: And you both keep your own scores as well as some third party.
sentences.zh: 你们俩既要记自己的分，也会有第三方来记分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's just kind of Scrabble rules.
sentences.zh: 这只是《拼词游戏》的规则之一。

sentences.en: And so, you can play out at the end of the game, you know, you know what your opponent has.
sentences.zh: 所以，在游戏结束时你可以打出来，你知道的，你知道你的对手有什么。

sentences.en: You know what they can spell.
sentences.zh: 你知道他们能拼出什么词。

sentences.en: And so, the obvious play for you at, like, a simple level is like, oh, I can score this many points.
sentences.zh: 所以，对你来说在一个简单层面上显而易见的走法是，哦，我可以得这么多分。

sentences.en: It's my best word.
sentences.zh: 这是我最好的词。

sentences.en: Could set them up to win the game in, like, some remarkable fashion.
sentences.zh: 这可能会以某种惊人的方式让他们赢得比赛。

sentences.en: So, you have to play out.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须把残局打完。

sentences.en: And depending on how many minutes you have left on your clock, because it's a timed game like chess as well,
sentences.zh: 取决于你的时钟上还剩多少分钟，因为这也是像国际象棋一样的计时赛，

sentences.en: you'll see someone sit there for seven minutes, finding the one path to, like, victory, which involves three different plays and, like, setting themselves up.
sentences.zh: 你会看到一个人坐在那里七分钟，寻找通往胜利的唯一途径，这涉及三种不同的下法以及如何为自己布局。

sentences.en: So, this is like, this is like end games in chess.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个有点像，这有点像国际象棋的残局。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Except that.
sentences.zh: 除了……

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, chess, I believe, is solved for any configuration of seven or eight pieces left on the board.
sentences.zh: 所以，国际象棋，我记得，棋盘上剩下七八个子的时候，任何配置都是有解的。

sentences.en: Computers have solved it.
sentences.zh: 计算机已经破解了。

sentences.en: Something like that, yeah.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧，对。

sentences.en: But Scrabble is more amenable to humans finding these paths, I guess, because it's – because there are a finite number of words in the dictionary,
sentences.zh: 但拼字游戏（Scrabble）更容易让人类找到这些路径，我猜，因为它是——因为字典里的单词数量是有限的，

sentences.en: in particular the two- and three-letter words that happen at the end.
sentences.zh: 特别是最后出现的两三个字母的单词。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I know that Quackle is a program that can solve end games perfectly up to a certain amount as well,
sentences.zh: 所以，对，我知道 Quackle 是一个也能在一定程度上完美解决残局的程序，

sentences.en: even though there's, I think, 135,000 words in the Scrabble dictionary.
sentences.zh: 尽管拼字游戏字典里我想有 135,000 个单词。

sentences.en: Depending on the dictionary you use, there's a Collins one and a North America one anyways.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你用的字典，反正有柯林斯版和北美版。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it is solvable, but it is – it's a lot harder to do.
sentences.zh: 但是，对，这是可解的，不过——做起来难得多。

sentences.en: Like, the best players in the world can do it.
sentences.zh: 比如，世界上最顶尖的玩家能做到这一点。

sentences.en: But there are some things that's incredibly hard to see.
sentences.zh: 但有些东西是极其难看出来的。

sentences.en: And another really, really cool trick,
sentences.zh: 还有一个非常非常酷的技巧，

sentences.en: like Jackson Smiley is a Canadian top world-ranked player that actually was on Jimmy Kimmel years ago on that little kid contest where they bring on the two young Scrabble players.
sentences.zh: 比如杰克逊·斯迈利（Jackson Smiley）是加拿大世界排名靠前的玩家，几年前曾上过吉米·坎摩尔（Jimmy Kimmel）的节目，参加那个汇聚了两位年轻拼字游戏玩家的小朋友竞赛。

sentences.en: He was – you know, when he was a kid, went on that program.
sentences.zh: 他——你知道，他小时候上过那个节目。

sentences.en: I think he's roughly my age, plus or minus.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他大概和我同龄，上下差不了几岁。

sentences.en: And he still plays now.
sentences.zh: 而且他现在还在玩。

sentences.en: But he is crazy for his setups that he will do where they know, oh, I have the only M left and I can hook this word with an M at the end.
sentences.zh: 但他对自己的布局简直狂热，他会做一些这样的局：他们知道，哦，我是唯一留着 M 的人，我可以把这个单词末尾连上一个 M。

sentences.en: So I will put it here.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它放在这儿。

sentences.en: It will be unblockable.
sentences.zh: 这就无解了，别人挡不住。

sentences.en: And then I'll wait.
sentences.zh: 然后我就等着。

sentences.en: And so it looks like he's just kind of playing a whatever – you know, other elite players will recognize this and try to block.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来他只是在随便玩——你知道，其他精英玩家会认出这一点并试图阻拦。

sentences.en: But they try to set up these situations where they've – they're putting something – they're basically laying themselves up or like for an alley-oop that is unblockable because they have the only tile left in the bag because they've been tracking.
sentences.zh: 但他们试图建立这种局面——他们正在放一些东西——他们基本上是在为一记无法阻挡的空中接力做铺垫，因为他们通过记牌，手里握着袋子里仅存的最后一块牌。

sentences.en: And every once in a while you'll see something like – I've seen before where someone played EAU, which is the French word for water, but it's in the Scrabble dictionary.
sentences.zh: 而且你偶尔会看到这样的情况——我以前见过，有人打出了 EAU，这是法语里“水”的意思，但它在拼字游戏词典里。

sentences.en: And they put that next to a triple letter.
sentences.zh: 他们把它放在三倍字数（triple letter）格子的旁边。

sentences.en: And E-A-U-X is also a word.
sentences.zh: 而且 E-A-U-X 也是一个词。

sentences.en: And they had the X on their rack.
sentences.zh: 他们的牌架上有 X。

sentences.en: So they were setting themselves up.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一直在给自己做局。

sentences.en: 30-odd points or – no, X is eight, right?
sentences.zh: 三十多分，还是——不对，X 是八分，对吧？

sentences.en: And EAU is one each.
sentences.zh: EAU 每个一分。

sentences.en: So it's X times three.
sentences.zh: 所以是 X 乘以三。

sentences.en: But then they played another word that ended in X.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们又打出了另一个以 X 结尾的单词。

sentences.en: So they spelt O that ended in X plus something like tax.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拼出了以 X 结尾的 O，外加诸如 tax 之类的词。

sentences.en: So you end up getting 48 points for that one letter.
sentences.zh: 因此你最终这单个字母能得到 48 分。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And – Because it's triple in both of the words.
sentences.zh: 而且——因为两个词都享受了三倍加成。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then it can look like – I mean, elite players, they automatically always recognize these things where, oh,
sentences.zh: 然后看起来可能会——我是说，精英玩家，他们总是能自动识别出这些事情，比如，哦，

sentences.en: they might be setting up a ZA dual direction triple play where you get 40 or 60 for 6 times 10 for Z or Z.
sentences.zh: 他们可能在布设一个 ZA 双向三倍连击，因为 Z 或 Z 的 6 乘以 10 能得到 40 或 60 分。

sentences.en: I don't actually know which one's American, but I know the Americans.
sentences.zh: 我其实不知道哪个是美式的，但我知道美式的。

sentences.en: Anyways.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: Z, Americans say Z, yeah.
sentences.zh: Z，美国人念 Z，对。

sentences.en: Z.
sentences.zh: Z。

sentences.en: But like elite players will see this immediately.
sentences.zh: 但精英玩家一眼就能看出来。

sentences.en: But if you're – if I'm just playing casually, like no one's going to notice that I dropped an A next to a triple and that I might have the Z on my rack.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是——如果我只是随便玩玩，比如没人会注意到我在三倍格子旁边下了一个 A，而且我的牌架上可能还有个 Z。

sentences.en: And – but they'll see this immediately.
sentences.zh: 而且——但他们一眼就能看出这一点。

sentences.en: And, you know, anyways, it's a very simple game in terms of like, oh, you just – it's a crossword game.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，总之，就……哦，这只是个填字游戏，从这个角度看它是个非常简单的游戏。

sentences.en: Speaking of which, we'll transition now an hour later.
sentences.zh: 说到这儿，我们一小时后切到下一个话题。

sentences.en: We've got two board game episodes now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有两期关于桌游的节目。

sentences.en: We're going to have to split this into two parts because –
sentences.zh: 我们得把它剪成两部分，因为——

sentences.en: Well, I just wanted to hook in also on the sort of algorithmic side of things.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只是想顺便切入算法那一方面。

sentences.en: Well, we'll save the books movie.
sentences.zh: 好吧，书和电影的先留着。

sentences.en: But I was going to say Ava and I, when we were dating, used to play Cribbage a bunch, which is a great game for two players.
sentences.zh: 不过我想说的是，我和爱娃（Ava）在约会的时候经常玩双陆棋（Cribbage），这是一款非常适合两人的游戏。

sentences.en: Cribbage and – there's another game that I get mixed up.
sentences.zh: 双陆棋和——还有另一个游戏我老搞混。

sentences.en: Is this the one with the 29 and the pegs on the board or –
sentences.zh: 是那个有 29 分和棋盘插钉的那个吗，还是——

sentences.en: Cribbage has – yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 双陆棋有——是的，没毛病。

sentences.en: So, yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，没错。

sentences.en: So, it – there's a – a Cribbage board has the pegs.
sentences.zh: 所以，它——一个双陆棋棋盘上有那些插钉。

sentences.en: You play to 121 and 29 is the highest scoring hand.
sentences.zh: 你们要玩到 121 分，而 29 是最高得分手牌。

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，对。

sentences.en: And you find some Cribbage boards that look like a 29.
sentences.zh: 你会发现有些双陆棋棋盘长得就像数字 29。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're commonly – you find the 29 shape.
sentences.zh: 它们通常——你会发现 29 形状的。

sentences.en: Cribbage scoring is very interesting algorithmically.
sentences.zh: 从算法角度来看，双陆棋的计分非常有趣。

sentences.en: It's – it's one of those things that I periodically go back to as sort of a coding practice, a coding exercise, is scoring a Cribbage hand because it's – like I say,
sentences.zh: 它是——这是我定期会回去当做编码练习、编码实操的一种东西，计算双陆棋手牌的分数，因为就像我说的，

sentences.en: it's algorithmically interesting.
sentences.zh: 它在算法上很有趣。

sentences.en: To begin with, there is a – there is an order in which you count up a Cribbage hand.
sentences.zh: 首先，计算双陆棋手牌有一个特定的顺序。

sentences.en: So, you're looking for, to begin with, cards that sum to 15.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先你要找的是加起来等于 15 的牌。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And your hand is four cards.
sentences.zh: 你的手牌是四张。

sentences.en: Your hand is four cards and there's an extra starter card, which you get to include in counting.
sentences.zh: 你的手牌是四张，还有一张额外的翻开牌（starter card），你在计分时可以把这张牌算进去。

sentences.en: There are various rules.
sentences.zh: 这里有各种规则。

sentences.en: So, to start with, you're looking for cards that sum to 15.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先你要寻找加起来等于 15 的牌。

sentences.en: Ace is always one, never 11.
sentences.zh: A 永远是 1，绝不是 11。

sentences.en: So, ace is always low in Cribbage.
sentences.zh: 所以，在双陆棋中 A 总是当作小牌（low）。

sentences.en: So, you're looking for 15s.
sentences.zh: 因此你要找凑成 15 的组合。

sentences.en: You're looking for pairs.
sentences.zh: 你要找对子。

sentences.en: You're looking for runs of three or more.
sentences.zh: 你要找三张或更多的顺子。

sentences.en: Runs, yeah.
sentences.zh: 顺子，对。

sentences.en: I remember that.
sentences.zh: 我记得这个。

sentences.en: And then you're looking for – there's a score called – one – it's called knobs, or I say one for his knob because that's the way I was taught, which is if you're holding a jack,
sentences.zh: 然后你要找的是——有一个分数叫做——一分——叫做 knobs，或者我习惯说“one for his knob”，因为我是这么被教的，意思是你手里拿着一个杰克（J），

sentences.en: which is the same suit as the starter card that got turned up, it scores one point.
sentences.zh: 它的花色和翻开的起始牌相同，这就得一分。

sentences.en: You can also, I think, score for a flush, although that's rarer.
sentences.zh: 我想你也可以因为同花（flush）而得分，尽管这比较少见。

sentences.en: But what makes Cribbage interesting to score is all of those things, but also the fact that it's combinatoric.
sentences.zh: 但让双陆棋计分变得有趣的是所有这些规则，还有它是组合数学（combinatoric）的事实。

sentences.en: So, the highest scoring hand is – you're holding a jack and three fives, and the turn-up card is a five of the same suit as your jack, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，最高得分的手牌是——你手里拿着一个 J 和三个 5，而翻出来的牌是和你手里 J 同花色的 5，对吧？

sentences.en: That hand scores 29.
sentences.zh: 那手牌能得 29 分。

sentences.en: And the way it scores 29 is by counting 15s combinatorically.
sentences.zh: 它得到 29 分的方式是通过组合数学来计算 15。
所以你有：15 算 2 分、15 算 4 分、15 算 6 分、15 算 8 分。

sentences.en: That's the jack paired with each of the fives.
sentences.zh: 那是 J 分别与每个 5 组成对子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's eight points.
sentences.zh: 那是八分。

sentences.en: Then you've got the four fives.
sentences.zh: 然后你有四个 5。

sentences.en: How many ways are there to select three from four?
sentences.zh: 从四个里面选出三个有多少种方法？

sentences.en: Because three fives are 15, right?
sentences.zh: 因为三个 5 等于 15，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like triangle building, right?
sentences.zh: 对，就像搭三角形一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: So, you've got however many there are there.
sentences.zh: 所以你有对应的那些组合数。

sentences.en: Then you've got all of the combinatorial pairs of fives.
sentences.zh: 然后你有了 5 的所有组合对子。

sentences.en: Again, you've got four fives.
sentences.zh: 同样，你有四个 5。

sentences.en: How many ways can you select a pair of fives?
sentences.zh: 选出一对 5 有多少种方法？

sentences.en: Score two points for every one.
sentences.zh: 每种得两分。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: This is what I mean.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的意思。

sentences.en: It's combinatorial.
sentences.zh: 这是组合数学。

sentences.en: And then finally, the one for knobs makes the score up to 29.
sentences.zh: 最后，“one for knobs”把总分凑到了 29。

sentences.en: That's the extra one point.
sentences.zh: 那就是额外的那一分。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is algorithmically interesting, but also it would be very – not monotonous.
sentences.zh: 对，这在算法上很有趣，但同时也会非常——倒也不是单调。

sentences.en: But I'm trying to think of like the elegant way and it's like, eh, there's probably going to be no array, single liner.
sentences.zh: 我在想那种优雅的写法，然后觉得，呃，可能不会有什么单行数组表达式（single liner）。

sentences.en: It's going to be a bunch of –
sentences.zh: 它会是一堆——

sentences.en: The elegant way to do it might be recursion.
sentences.zh: 优雅的实现方式可能是递归。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's the way I normally do it.
sentences.zh: 我通常都是这么做的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: At first, until it was the example, I was thinking of like the 7, 8, 6, 7, 8, 9 hand, which usually was what I was shooting for.
sentences.zh: 一开始，在看到那个例子之前，我想到的是像 7、8、6、7、8、9 这样的手牌，这通常是我在追求的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because that's also a decent hand that has the 7, 8, 6, 9.
sentences.zh: 因为那也是一手相当不错的手牌，包含了 7、8、6、9。

sentences.en: A very good hand is like – especially if you have, say,
sentences.zh: 一手非常好的牌就像是——特别是如果你有，比方说，

sentences.en: 6, 7, 7, 8, and you get a 9 turned up, right?
sentences.zh: 6、7、7、8，然后翻出来一张 9，对吧？

sentences.en: As soon as you get a double 7 in there or a double 8, then the combinatorics starts to come into play because you've got 15, 2 with 7 and 8, 15, 4 with the other 7 and
sentences.zh: 一旦你里面有了双 7 或双 8，组合数学就开始发挥作用了，因为你有 7 和 8 组成的 15 算 2 分，另一个 7 和 8 组成的 15 算 4 分，

sentences.en: 8, 15, 6 with the 6 and 9.
sentences.zh: 还有 6 和 9 组成的 15 算 6 分。

sentences.en: Then you've got the runs.
sentences.zh: 然后你有顺子。

sentences.en: And again, you're counting the runs combinatorically.
sentences.zh: 同样，你是用组合数学来数顺子的。

sentences.en: So, 6, 7, 8, 9 is one run.
sentences.zh: 所以，6、7、8、9 是一个顺子。

sentences.en: And then 6 other 7, 8, 9 is the other run.
sentences.zh: 然后另一个 7、6、8、9 是另一个顺子。

sentences.en: And you've got the pair of 7s as well.
sentences.zh: 你还有一个双 7 的对子。

sentences.en: So, you've got a lot of different scoring in there once you start doubling up.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你开始翻倍，里面就会有很多不同的得分。

sentences.en: You know, because the 7 is doubled as part of a 15 and also doubled as part of a run.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为 7 既是 15 的一部分被重复计算，又是顺子的一部分被重复计算。

sentences.en: It's multiplying up.
sentences.zh: 它在成倍增长。

sentences.en: So, I'm actually trying to think, though, is that – could you solve it by doing a – is it permutations?
sentences.zh: 所以我其实在想，这是——你能通过做一个——是排列（permutations）吗？

sentences.en: So, no, it's not permutations.
sentences.zh: 所以，不是，不是排列。

sentences.en: It's power set.
sentences.zh: 是幂集（power set）。

sentences.en: Permutation – so, combinations is – order doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 排列——所以，组合是——顺序不重要。

sentences.en: Permutations, order matters.
sentences.zh: 排列，顺序很重要。

sentences.en: Power set is all the lengths up to N.
sentences.zh: 幂集是长度达到 N 的所有子集。

sentences.en: So, the question is, if you took the power set – I think it's – and it might actually need to be the permutations of each – well, actually, no, I don't think permutations matters
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，如果你取幂集——我想是这样的——而且实际上可能需要每个的排列——不过，其实，不，我觉得排列不重要，

sentences.en: because the order of the cards definitely doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 因为牌的顺序绝对不重要。

sentences.en: You just can keep them in sorted order to check for runs.
sentences.zh: 你只要把它们保持排序状态来检查顺子就行了。

sentences.en: If you took the power set of the four cards you had, which for four is not going to explode that big, could you solve it that way?
sentences.zh: 如果你取你拥有的四张牌的幂集——对于四张牌来说不会爆炸得太大，你能用这种方法解决吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's – but it's five.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它是——但这是五张。

sentences.en: The fifth card can be included if needed.
sentences.zh: 如果有需要，第五张牌可以包含进来。

sentences.en: That's one of the things that puts a wrinkle in it.
sentences.zh: 这就是让事情变得棘手的地方之一。

sentences.en: Like, for example, you can have a flush if all the cards in your hand are the same suit, and that scores four points.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你手里的牌花色都一样，你就能得到同花，这能得四分。

sentences.en: If the card that gets turned up is also that same suit, you can score five points, right?
sentences.zh: 如果翻出来的牌也是同一种花色，你就能得五分，对吧？

sentences.en: Likewise, the card that gets turned up may or may not be included in a run, depending on whether – if you have a run of three in your hand, that's sufficient.
sentences.zh: 同样，翻出来的牌可能会也可能不会被包含在顺子中，这取决于——如果你手里有一个三张的顺子，那就够了。

sentences.en: But if you can make a run of four, you can do that too, for example.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能凑成一个四张的顺子，比如你也可以这样做。

sentences.en: Oh, but you won't get points for a run of three if there's the run of four as well.
sentences.zh: 噢，但如果有四张连牌的话，三张连牌可就没分了。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So that breaks my power set model that I was trying to think if, like, if you could just create every combination of, like, length two, three, and four from your four, can you
sentences.zh: 这打破了我的幂集模型，我之前还在想，比如说，如果你能用你的四张牌创造出所有长度为二、三和四的组合，你能

sentences.en: map the points uniquely to each one of those and then just sum it up?
sentences.zh: 把这些分数唯一地映射到每一个组合上，然后把它们加起来吗？

sentences.en: Oh, that's right.
sentences.zh: 噢，对哦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, the run length does not apply combinatorically.
sentences.zh: 对，顺子的长度不适用于组合计算。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The contents of the run would.
sentences.zh: 顺子的内容适用。

sentences.en: You're swapping out cards and whatever.
sentences.zh: 你在换牌之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a very interesting problem to code up.
sentences.zh: 对，编写这段代码是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: And it's interesting also just – so there's an algorithmically interesting part, and then
sentences.zh: 而且这也很有趣——所以有一个算法上很有趣的部分，然后

sentences.en: there's a sort of code design part, which is how you represent the cards, how you represent
sentences.zh: 有一个代码设计的部分，也就是你如何表示牌，你如何表示

sentences.en: the hands, how you represent the deck and dealing the hands, which applies in generally to card games, I think.

sentences.en: Tony's famous question.
sentences.zh: 托尼的著名问题。

sentences.en: Link to Tony's – one of Tony's talks.
sentences.zh: 链接到托尼的——托尼的演讲之一。

sentences.en: I like the way in array programming, it's a pretty classic trick.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢数组编程中的这种方式，这是一个相当经典的技巧。

sentences.en: You just assign 1 to 52 or 0 to 51 if you want to – depending on your array language.
sentences.zh: 如果你想的话，只需分配 1 到 52 或 0 到 51——取决于你的数组语言。

sentences.en: I think 0 to 51 works a little bit nicer, though, because you can then do immediately mod 13.
sentences.zh: 不过，我觉得 0 到 51 稍微好用一点，因为你可以立即进行模 13 运算。

sentences.en: So you do mod 13 to get suits.
sentences.zh: 所以你做模 13 运算来获取花色。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And because you have – I'm sure you could do this in other languages, but it's really easy to do in array languages.
sentences.zh: 因为你有——我相信你在其他语言中也能做到这一点，但在数组语言中这真的很容易。

sentences.en: You can do this index selection where you create a string of the Unicode diamonds, hearts, spades, and clubs.
sentences.zh: 你可以进行这种索引选择，创建一个包含 Unicode 方块、红桃、黑桃和梅花的字符串。

sentences.en: And then you can just – mod 13, you can go integer division and then index into – so like if you have 16, which will be, I don't know, like the seven of hearts or something.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以——模 13，你可以进行整数除法，然后索引到——比如说如果你有 16，大概是，我不知道，比如红桃七什么的。

sentences.en: Or actually, no, it's going to be lower than that, the three of hearts or something.
sentences.zh: 或者其实，不对，它会比那个小，比如红桃三什么的。

sentences.en: And then you integer divide that by 13, you'll get one.
sentences.zh: 然后你把它整除以 13，你就会得到一。

sentences.en: And then you can index into your length four string of those Unicode symbols.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以索引到你那四个字符长度的 Unicode 符号字符串中。

sentences.en: And so like in a few characters by using just 0 to 51, I mean, this breaks the whole using a value versus et cetera that Tony talks about.
sentences.zh: 所以，通过只使用 0 到 51，只需几个字符，我的意思是，这打破了托尼所谈论的整个使用值类型与引用类型等的问题。

sentences.en: But it's a super fast way to get like a card game going and to display things in a terminal that look quite nice.
sentences.zh: 但这是快速启动一个纸牌游戏并在终端中显示相当好看的界面的超级快的方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's cool.
sentences.zh: 对，这很酷。

sentences.en: I mean, you also need to deal with like court cards all counting 10 as far as the 15s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你还需要处理人头牌在计算 15 点时全都算作 10 点的情况。

sentences.en: That's another, you know, the value of the card is not the value of the card.
sentences.zh: 那是另一个，你知道的，牌的面值并不是牌的点数。

sentences.en: For the pip cards it is, but for the picture cards, they're all 10, right?
sentences.zh: 对于点数牌是这样的，但对于花牌，它们全都是 10，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So when you're counting 15s, you need to take care of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以当你计算 15 点时，你需要处理这类事情。

sentences.en: So there are enough sort of special case rules like that to make it interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以有足够多这样的特殊规则，让它变得有趣。

sentences.en: It's not terribly complex, but it is more complex than simply power setting the cards, right?
sentences.zh: 它并不是极其复杂，但比单纯对牌进行幂集运算要复杂，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Maybe we should have a whole other episode on it.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该专门做一整期节目来聊这个。

sentences.zh: 因为我记得我刚爱上编程时做的最早的事情之一，因为我在学校里学的是精算相关的东西。

sentences.en: I had to take two programming courses.
sentences.zh: 我必须修两门编程课。

sentences.zh: 而我上的第一门课其实学得很艰难。

sentences.en: It was a Python course, just intro to CS.
sentences.zh: 那是一门 Python 课，只是计算机科学导论。

sentences.en: And I was never the best student.
sentences.zh: 我从来都不是最好的学生。

sentences.en: I kind of skated through high school.
sentences.zh: 我在高中时有点混日子。

sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果有些事情不能立刻被我理解，我就会想，啊，这不适合我。

sentences.en: And I was like, this can't be that hard.
sentences.zh: 我想，这不可能那么难吧。

sentences.en: And so I actually sat down, tried to figure out, you know, for loops of statements and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的坐下来，试图弄明白，你知道的，for 循环、语句之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then I was like, wait a second, like, I did the assignment.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，等一下，我把作业做完了。

sentences.en: I was like, with these, like, couple tools, you could do, you could do anything.
sentences.zh: 我想，有了这几个工具，你就能做到，你就能做到任何事情。

sentences.en: And then, like, the next two to three days, like, disappeared.
sentences.zh: 然后，接下来的两到三天就像，消失了一样。

sentences.en: And I wrote this, like, 3000 line poker simulation.
sentences.zh: 我写了一个大约 3000 行的扑克模拟程序。

sentences.en: Because at the time, I was a big fan of poker, not gambling, because I couldn't gamble yet.
sentences.zh: 因为当时我是扑克的超级粉丝，不是指赌博，因为我当时还不能赌博。

sentences.en: I was too young.
sentences.zh: 我太年轻了。

sentences.en: That's a whole different story.
sentences.zh: 那是完全不同的另一个故事了。

sentences.en: I don't gamble anymore.
sentences.zh: 我现在不赌博了。

sentences.en: Probability.

sentences.en: Yeah, statistics, money.

sentences.zh: 我真希望我能把那段代码找出来。

sentences.zh: 它在某个地方的某个硬盘上。

sentences.zh: 我想很多学生也是这样。

sentences.zh: 我记得有一次我帮助一个做扑克作业的人，当我在用 Elixir 时，他们被惊艳到了——他们当时在使用 Elixir。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, yeah, Elixir has all this stuff, you know, chunk by, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，哦，对，Elixir 有所有这些东西，你知道的，比如 chunk by 之类的。

sentences.en: And they were like, what the heck?
sentences.zh: 他们当时就想，什么鬼？

sentences.en: I was just going to loop through this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我本来打算用循环来遍历这些东西呢。

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, that's exactly how I would have thought when I was first learning it.
sentences.zh: 我说，对，这正是我刚开始学的时候的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 我有一个类似的经历。

sentences.en: Jason would say there's a difference between those – was Yahtzee.
sentences.zh: 杰森会说这两者有区别——那就是快艇骰子游戏（Yahtzee）。

sentences.en: I wrote a Yahtzee program that I spent a whole summer playing with my brother and sister.
sentences.zh: 我写了一个 Yahtzee 程序，花了我整个夏天的时间和我的兄弟姐妹一起玩。

sentences.en: We would play together and, you know, it was the whole game, so it rolled the dice and then
sentences.zh: 我们会一起玩，你知道的，那是整个游戏，所以它会掷骰子，然后

sentences.en: you could choose where to put the score and hold and all that, you know, the play of Yahtzee.
sentences.zh: 你可以选择把分数放在哪里、保留哪些骰子等等，你知道的，Yahtzee 的玩法。

sentences.en: I see you have Yahtzee behind you there.
sentences.zh: 我看到你身后就放着 Yahtzee。

sentences.en: I love – Yahtzee is my favorite party game.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢——Yahtzee 是我最喜欢的聚会游戏。

sentences.en: It's another game where there is a hidden strategy, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是另一个包含隐藏策略的游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: I think that's beyond the surface meaning of the game, if you like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，我认为这超出了游戏的表面意义。

sentences.en: Because, you know, as a kid learning Yahtzee, I didn't fully understand that one of the strategies is like, you know, you roll the dice and you get a certain score, right?
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，作为一个学习 Yahtzee 的孩子，我并没有完全理解其中一个策略是，你知道的，你掷骰子然后得到一定的分数，对吧？

sentences.en: You get a certain outcome.
sentences.zh: 你得到了某个结果。

sentences.en: And then you can choose where to score those dice, right?
sentences.zh: 然后你可以选择把这些骰子的分数记在哪个记分格里，对吧？

sentences.en: And you don't have to score them in places where they obviously score or places that you were going for, right?
sentences.zh: 你不需要把它们记在那些明显得分的地方，或者你原本想要的目标地方，对吧？

sentences.en: If they come out bad, you could choose to take a zero in the ones, for example, right?
sentences.zh: 如果骰子点数不好，你可以选择在“1”这一栏记零分，例如，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the most you can ever get in the ones is five.
sentences.zh: 因为在“1”这一栏你最多只能得到五分。

sentences.en: Or five, yeah.
sentences.zh: 或者五分，对。

sentences.en: With the bonus Yahtzee, admittedly.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是加上奖励 Yahtzee 的情况。

sentences.en: But four, let's say.
sentences.zh: 但比如说四分。

sentences.en: The most you're likely to get in the ones is four.
sentences.zh: 你在“1”这一栏最可能得到的最高分是四分。

sentences.en: So I had not appreciated that whole level of strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时并没有领会到那一整个层面的策略。

sentences.en: When I first started playing Yahtzee at the age of eight or whatever.
sentences.zh: 当我八岁左右刚开始玩 Yahtzee 的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Yahtzee is a game that is mostly luck.
sentences.zh: Yahtzee 是一个主要靠运气的游戏。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's 90-10 luck and skill, but I love Yahtzee.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是不是 90% 的运气和 10% 的技巧，但我真的很喜欢 Yahtzee。

sentences.en: Typically, it's like a New Year's Eve party game where there's lots of people.
sentences.zh: 通常，它就像是一个有很多人的新年前夜派对游戏。

sentences.en: And I also, too, like my strategy is like I throw full houses.
sentences.zh: 而且我也一样，我的策略就是我总是去掷满堂红。

sentences.en: I don't care if it's my second.
sentences.zh: 我才不管这是不是我的第二轮。

sentences.en: I'm always going for Yahtzee.
sentences.zh: 我总是冲着 Yahtzee 去的。

sentences.en: It's like I want the 500-point game.
sentences.zh: 就像我想要那个 500 分的游戏一样。

sentences.en: I think I scored 450 one time.
sentences.zh: 我想我曾经得过 450 分。

sentences.en: But that, admittedly, is like every opportunity I have to get a Yahtzee, I'm going to take it.
sentences.zh: 但必须承认的是，只要有机会得到 Yahtzee，我都会抓住它。

sentences.en: Because even if there's a one in 216, whatever six to the power of three is, I still have a shot.
sentences.zh: 因为即使概率是 216 分之一（也就是 6 的 3 次方），我仍然有机会。

sentences.en: And it's worth the 100-point bonus to me to end up with 170, which is not a great score.
sentences.zh: 为了最终得到 170 分（这其实不是什么好分数），能拿到 100 分的奖励对我来说是值得的。

sentences.en: To end up with a game once every 20 games that's like 400-plus.
sentences.zh: 为了每 20 局能有一次像 400 分以上的高分。

sentences.en: Which is like three or four Yahtzees.
sentences.zh: 这就相当于三到四个 Yahtzee。

sentences.en: Because it's worth it to suffer through 19 games to have this one glorious moment.
sentences.zh: 因为为了这一个辉煌的时刻，忍受 19 局的痛苦是完全值得的。

sentences.en: And it usually doesn't go well.

sentences.zh: 但总有那么一天，那是美好的一天。

sentences.zh: 对，总有那么一天，一切都刚刚好。
